source.name: AI Daily
source.note: Every morning AI Daily's papers job reads the arXiv listings in cs.AI, cs.CL, cs.LG, cs.CV, cs.AR and cs.DC, keeps the papers with a data-center-scale or frontier-AI bearing (a keyword gate, then a Claude Haiku gate) and extracts the area, the headline benchmark with its baseline and result, a compute bucket, the scale, what was released, a one-line why-it-matters and a 1 to 5 importance. Those fields are a model's reading of the abstract: leads to check against the paper, never sources.

areas.name: Reasoning & agents
areas.description: Chain-of-thought, planning, tool use, agents and the test-time compute behind them.

areas.name: Architectures & training
areas.description: New model shapes, training recipes, scaling laws and the data that feeds them.

areas.name: Inference efficiency
areas.description: Serving cost: quantization, sparsity, speculative decoding, caching, kernels and the hardware they run on.

areas.name: Multimodal
areas.description: Vision, audio, video and models that read and write more than text.

areas.name: Alignment & safety
areas.description: Making models do what is meant: preference training, interpretability, red-teaming and evaluations of risk.

areas.name: Evaluation & benchmarks
areas.description: How capability is measured: new benchmarks, contamination, and what the leaderboards miss.

windows.name: This week
windows.description: Submitted to arXiv in the last seven days: the page is news, and nobody has replicated anything yet.

windows.name: This month
windows.description: Eight to thirty days old: early reactions, a code release or a second version may already be out.

windows.name: Back catalogue
windows.description: Older than a month: enough time to ask what happened next, who built on it and whether it held.

lenses.name: The one number
lenses.description: The headline result against its baseline: what the benchmark measures, how big the gain is in plain terms, whether the baseline is the strongest fair one, and what the number does not say.

lenses.name: What it costs
lenses.description: The compute, chips, energy and money behind the result, and what it would cost to use: tie the paper to the data centers, power and hardware AI Daily tracks.

lenses.name: Who built it
lenses.description: The lab or the lecture hall: who wrote it, with what resources, what they released (weights, code, data) and what that says about where frontier research now happens.

lenses.name: Hype check
lenses.description: The claims in the title and abstract against what the experiments show: the settings, the cherry-picks, contamination risk, and how the paper is being described outside arXiv.

lenses.name: Where it fits
lenses.description: The lineage: the two or three papers it builds on or argues with, what changed, and where this line of work is heading.

lenses.name: If it works
lenses.description: Take the result at face value and follow it out: who would use it, what it would change for the people who build, buy or are affected by AI, and what has to happen first.

lenses.name: Explain like I'm 5
lenses.description: The idea told to a five-year-old as a short picture story: one everyday stand-in, what the researchers figured out, and where the picture stops being true.
